children: Cryptocurrencies slumped on Friday as expectations of higher rates and the technology stock selloff sapped risk appetite.

Bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time since August, sinking 4% and putting the crypto benchmark on track for its sixth weekly loss, LSEG data show. It is now down over 21% from the highs reached in late September.
Ethereum breached key levels as well, crashing well past $2,000 to trade at three-month lows.
Bitcoin was last down 3.8% at $68,781, while Ethereum shed 4.3% to $1,927.
The selloff pours cold water on hopes that the crypto rebound that had begun during the summer is taking hold.
The backdrop for a crypto turnaround looks bleak: Stubbornly high U.S. inflation has markets pricing in more interest-rate hikes by the Federal Reserve, dimming the appeal of nonyielding assets.
The hawkish pivot in market pricing has also fueled strength in the dollar, creating another headwind for bitcoin demand.
A continued downturn in tech and artificial-intelligence stocks adds pressure too as traders liquidate positions to cover losses elsewhere.

"ETF outflows and other crypto-specific pressures, namely the fact that MSCI has confirmed it is removing Strategy from its indices, are also weighing," said Nic Puckrin, cross-asset analyst and founder of Coin Bureau.
The next potential stressor lies in U.S. economic data.

A hotter producer-price index reading could reinforce expectations of tighter monetary policy, extending ETF outflows, said Ranim Turfa, head of research and market analysis MENA at Tickmill. Softer numbers could help bitcoin stabilize, Turfa said.

title: Bitcoin Slides Past $70,000 as Risk-Off Mood Pressures Crypto
